description:
In `src/ocaml/lib/ai_linter/crystal_rules.ml`, inside `detect_long_method`, the local helper `count_nodes` is defined **twice** (lines 677 and 695). The first definition is more complete; the second shadows it.

**First definition (line 677) — complete:**
Handles EBlock, ELet, EIf, ECase, EApp, **ETryCatchFinally** (recursing into try_body, each rescue_body, ensure_body, else_body), and falls through to `1` for anything else.

**Second definition (line 695) — incomplete:**
Handles EBlock, EApp, EIf, ELet, ECase, and falls through to `1` for everything else. **It has no ETryCatchFinally case** — try/catch/ensure/else bodies are counted as a single node each instead of being walked.

**Consequence:** Functions whose body is an EBlock that includes a try/catch will be undercounted. A 100-node function with heavy try/catch will look like ~10 nodes, bypassing the `max_nodes = 80` threshold. False negatives in long-method detection for code that actually exercises the rescue/ensure/else arms.

**Fix:**
- Delete the second definition (lines 695-707)
- Keep the first, more complete version

This ticket is a child of catseye-ozj (the refactor epic) but can land independently.
title: BUG: count_nodes in detect_long_method defined twice — second version misses ETryCatchFinally
